heading: INT. SMALL CLAIMS COURT, STRIKE ZONE LANES ANNEX - DAY

units.text: INT. SMALL CLAIMS COURT, STRIKE ZONE LANES ANNEX - DAY
A bowling alley, daytime.
A folding table stands at the end of lane four.
The pins are still set.
A hand-lettered sign: "COURT IN SESSION.
NO SHOES, NO SERVICE."
JUDGE FAIRCLOTH, sixties, in a black robe over a bowling shirt, sits on a high stool.
ELSPETH MORROW, forties, the plaintiff, stands with a binder.
MR. ABERNATHY, seventies, the defendant, sits in a plastic chair clutching a trophy.
Ms. Morrow, you allege Mr. Abernathy broke your window with a bowling ball.
units.name: FAIRCLOTH

units.text: I allege it, Your Honor. Lane six, left-hand hook, two a.m.
units.name: ELSPETH

units.text: It wasn't two. It was one-forty.
units.name: ABERNATHY

units.text: Mr. Abernathy, you'll have your turn.
units.name: FAIRCLOTH

units.text: One-forty. I wrote it down.
units.name: ABERNATHY

units.text: The ball came through my bathroom window, Your Honor.
units.name: ELSPETH

units.text: From the alley?
units.name: FAIRCLOTH

units.text: From the parking lot. He was bowling in the parking lot.
units.name: ELSPETH

units.text: Abernathy grips the trophy.
Faircloth leans down from the stool and gestures with his gavel to the empty lanes beyond, as if the gallery were full.
Let the record show we have no jury, no clerk, and no coffee.
units.name: FAIRCLOTH

units.text: He taps the gavel.
It bounces off the table and rolls under lane four.
